records.summary: The records show 2650 Ocean Ave is in the NCD-Lakeside Village zoning district, where a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted. The site is also within the Family and Senior Housing Opportunity Special Use District. No prior applications or permits appear on file at this exact address or parcel (7223/004). The immediate block is an established restaurant corridor: within 500 feet there are 6 registered food/drink businesses and 3 active ABC Type 41 licenses (beer-and-wine restaurants). The surrounding Ocean Avenue addresses show a 30-year pattern of restaurant approvals—mostly change-of-ownership referrals—with no use decisions denied within 1,000 feet in the available records.

Zero use decisions for restaurants found within 1,000 feet in the last 10 years (N=0); too few for a meaningful approval rate

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant 40 meters away in the same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning district, approved in 2019 via Health Department referral for a simple limited restaurant use—the closest match to the concept's limited cooking designation.
comparables.key_takeaway: This agency referral imposed an 11 p.m. closing condition citing Planning Code Section 716, showing that even a principally permitted limited restaurant can carry an hours restriction when routed through Health rather than approved by right at the building permit stage.

comparables.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant with ABC Type 41 beer-and-wine license immediately adjacent (12 meters away, 2642 Ocean Ave) in identical zoning, approved January 2023—the most recent decision on this block and directly next door to the subject site.
comparables.key_takeaway: This ABC agency referral was approved in 19 days with no conditions, citing restaurant use as permitted under Planning Code Section 727. The speed and lack of conditions reflect routine treatment of restaurant continuation in this corridor, though formula retail was explicitly noted as not permitted.

comparables.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant (Lucho's) with ABC Type 41 at 2675 Ocean Ave (53 meters away), same zoning district, approved May 2021 as a continuation with beer-and-wine service—demonstrates recent approval pattern for alcohol-serving restaurants on this block.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days citing Planning Code Sections 710 and 202.2(a) eating/drinking use conditions. The reference to Section 202.2(a) signals that even routine approvals invoke the standard restaurant operating conditions (trash, noise, queuing) in NCD districts.

comparables.why_comparable: The only use decision (Conditional Use Authorization) found among the candidates, approved in 1988 at 2642–2646 Ocean Ave (12 meters away, same parcel as the 2023 ABC referral) to expand a small fast-food restaurant into a large fast-food restaurant in the then-NC-1 district.
comparables.key_takeaway: A CUA was required 36 years ago to create a large fast-food restaurant at this exact neighboring address. No conditions were extracted, and the use has continued through multiple ownership changes since. This signals that once a restaurant use is established via CUA or by right, changes of ownership are handled as routine agency referrals.

comparables.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant (Lucho's) at 2675 Ocean Ave (53 meters), approved September 2018 via Health referral for continuation of use, same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning—shows the corridor's stable restaurant character and referral process.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in one day, citing Planning Code Sections 710 and 202.2(a). The one-day turnaround for a Health Department sign-off underscores that established restaurant uses on Ocean Avenue face minimal Planning review when there is no change of use or expansion.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant (My Cup of Tea) at 2660 Ocean Ave (36 meters away), approved November 2017 as a change-of-ownership continuation in NCD-Lakeside Village zoning, no alcohol, demonstrating treatment of non-alcohol restaurant transitions.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 17 days with no extracted conditions, described as 'continuation of existing use, change of ownership only.' This confirms that non-alcohol restaurants moving into established restaurant spaces receive swift, unconditioned approvals on this corridor.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant (Ocean Thai) at 2545 Ocean Ave (124 meters), approved February 2018 as continuation of a restaurant use established in 2002, same NCD-Lakeside Village zoning, illustrating long-term restaurant precedent along the broader Ocean Avenue corridor.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in two days, explicitly referencing the original 2002 permit (MB0200855). The multi-decade continuity of restaurant uses on Ocean Avenue and the speed of change-of-ownership approvals demonstrate Planning's comfort with the restaurant corridor character.

patterns.pattern: All restaurant applications on Ocean Avenue in NCD-Lakeside Village since 2001 visible in the records were approved, with zero denials or withdrawals found within 1,000 feet. The corridor shows a 30-year pattern of uninterrupted restaurant approvals.

Agency referrals (Health Department, ABC) for continuation or change-of-ownership of existing restaurant uses are approved in 1–30 days with no substantive conditions. These are administrative sign-offs, not discretionary hearings.

Limited restaurant approvals can carry an 11 p.m. closing-hour condition under Planning Code Section 716 when routed through Health Department plan review, even though the underlying use is principally permitted in NCD zoning.

Planning Code Section 202.2(a) eating and drinking use conditions (addressing trash, noise, odor, and customer queuing) are routinely cited in NCD-Lakeside Village restaurant approvals, signaling that standard operating conditions apply even to principally permitted uses.

Formula retail is explicitly flagged as not permitted in NCD-Lakeside Village in recent ABC referrals, confirming that independent restaurants are the expected use and chains would require separate review.

ABC Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) licenses are approved as a matter of course for bona fide restaurants in NCD-Lakeside Village, with approvals citing Planning Code Sections 710, 727, or 790.92 and no additional zoning conditions beyond the eating/drinking use standards.

The immediately adjacent parcel (2642–2646 Ocean Ave, 12 meters away) has operated continuously as a restaurant since a 1988 CUA for a large fast-food restaurant, with at least seven subsequent change-of-ownership approvals through 2023, demonstrating stable restaurant use next door.

risk.concept_summary: A 4,440-square-foot restaurant with limited cooking, no alcohol, five employees, tenant improvements, and exterior signage at 2650 Ocean Ave in the NCD-Lakeside Village zoning district.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether the space was last used as a restaurant or similar food use and whether the business is an independent or part of a chain, then file the Conditional Use Authorization if required.

approvals.summary: A Conditional Use Authorization is required because the restaurant exceeds 3,000 square feet (Planning Code Section 727 size threshold). Formula retail, laundromat removal, and operating hours remain undecided due to missing information about chain affiliation, prior use, and closing time.

findings.text: In NCD-Lakeside Village zoning a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted, but a use of 3,000 square feet or more requires Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code Section 727, in force on 12 February 2024), and this concept is 4,440 square feet.

The records show no prior applications or permits at 2650 Ocean Ave or on parcel 7223/004, and no active ABC license of a type the rules read is on file, so the records do not establish what the space was last used as.

The immediately adjacent address (2642 Ocean Ave, 12 meters away) has operated continuously as a restaurant since a 1988 Conditional Use Authorization for a large fast-food restaurant, with the most recent ABC Type 41 approval in January 2023 approved in 19 days with no conditions.

All seven visible restaurant applications in NCD-Lakeside Village zoning within 1,000 feet since 1988 were approved; zero were denied or withdrawn (N = 7 approved agency referrals and use decisions; the base rate excludes these as too few to show).

Formula retail is not permitted in NCD-Lakeside Village (Planning Code Section 727). The 2023 ABC referral at 2642 Ocean Ave explicitly noted that formula retail is not permitted, confirming that independent restaurants are expected and chains would face a prohibition or require separate review.

Six registered food and drink businesses operate within 500 feet (Bay Pocha, My Cup of Tea, Yy Coffee & Tea, Lucho's, Ocean Thai, Ofena), and three active ABC Type 41 licenses (beer-and-wine eating places) are on file at 2642, 2675, and 2545 Ocean Ave, establishing a dense restaurant corridor.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is required and is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing, so it is allowed once the prerequisites are met.

findings.text: A food or drink business in San Francisco needs a health permit to operate, issued by the Department of Public Health after plan review and final inspection (California Retail Food Code Sections 114380–114381; San Francisco Health Code Article 8).

A limited restaurant approval at 2620 Ocean Ave (40 meters away) in March 2019 carried an 11 p.m. closing-hour condition under Planning Code Section 716 when routed through the Health Department for a simple limited restaurant use, showing that hours can be conditioned even for principally permitted uses.

The health permit application is sent to the Planning Department for zoning review (San Francisco Planning Department Interagency Permit Referrals handout, March 2022), so the permit-to-operate step does not bypass the zoning determination.

approvals.summary: The building permit and change-of-use determination is insufficient information because the records do not show what the space was last used as, whether the occupant load is under 50, or the existing occupancy group, all of which only plans or an inspection can establish.

findings.text: Tenant improvements are planned, so a building permit is required from the Department of Building Inspection, and the permit application is sent to Planning for zoning review (Planning Code Section 175(a)).

Under the Building Code a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, but a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B (California Building Code 2022, Sections 303.1.1, 303.3). The description does not state whether occupancy is under 50, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it, and the records do not show what the space was last used as, so whether this is a change of occupancy or a change of use under the Planning Code is not established.

The limited cooking designation (small plates, reheating, panini) will require a commercial kitchen hood, grease interceptor, and Public Health plan check with DBI routing (San Francisco Public Utilities Commission FOG Ordinance; DPH plan-check fees).

expected_conditions.condition: Operating hours limited to 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily if Planning applies the principally permitted hours for NCD-Lakeside Village (Planning Code Section 727) or the limited-restaurant hours rule (Section 716).
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code Section 727 sets principally permitted restaurant hours at 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. in NCD-Lakeside Village, with 11 p.m. to 2 a.m. requiring Conditional Use. A limited restaurant at 2620 Ocean Ave (40 meters away) was conditioned to close by 11 p.m. under Section 716 in 2019, showing that hours are actively enforced for new limited restaurants on this block.

expected_conditions.condition: Standard eating and drinking use conditions under Planning Code Section 202.2(a): maintain a litter-free sidewalk, prevent odor and noise nuisance, manage customer queuing, and comply with all health and building codes.
expected_conditions.basis: Two recent ABC referrals for restaurants at 2675 Ocean Ave (2018 and 2021) explicitly cited Planning Code Section 202.2(a), which imposes general operating conditions on all eating and drinking establishments in Neighborhood Commercial districts. These conditions are applied even to principally permitted and continuation-of-use approvals.

expected_conditions.condition: Compliance with the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) Control Ordinance: install and maintain a grease interceptor sized to SFPUC standards, and submit the Installation Verification Form before final building sign-off.
expected_conditions.basis: Limited cooking (small plates, reheating, panini) produces fats, oils, and grease. The FOG Ordinance requires every food service establishment that cooks to install grease-capturing equipment before opening, and SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category that dictates the device type. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final approval.

expected_conditions.condition: Post the Department of Public Health permit to operate in a conspicuous location visible to the public, maintain a certified food safety manager on staff at all times, and ensure all food handlers obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire.
expected_conditions.basis: California Retail Food Code Section 113947.1 requires at least one certified food protection manager per facility, and Section 113948 requires every food handler to obtain a card within 30 days. Health inspectors verify these at the pre-opening inspection and at annual inspections.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether the space was last used as a restaurant, whether a Conditional Use Authorization is required, and whether formula retail or the laundromat-removal rule applies.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you are planning a 4,440-square-foot limited-cooking restaurant at 2650 Ocean Ave (parcel 7223/004) in NCD-Lakeside Village zoning, that the records show no prior use on file, and that you need written confirmation of (1) the prior use, (2) whether the size triggers a CUA, (3) whether formula retail applies if the business is independent, and (4) whether Planning Code Section 202.12 (laundromat removal) applies through 20 December 2024. Request a determination letter citing the applicable code sections and the prior-use finding.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application (Planning Code Section 303) with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, floor plans, a neighborhood outreach summary, and the filing fee.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe the concept as an independent limited-cooking restaurant (small plates, reheating, no full-service kitchen) serving approximately [occupant load] patrons with operating hours of 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, no alcohol, background music only, and no entertainment. Emphasize that the use is principally permitted under Section 727 and that the CUA is sought solely for the size threshold. Reference the continuous restaurant corridor on Ocean Avenue (2642, 2660, 2675 Ocean Ave) and commit to the standard eating/drinking conditions of Section 202.2(a): litter control, noise management, odor suppression, and customer queuing. State that the project will create no parking demand beyond existing neighborhood commercial patterns and that tenant improvements will comply with all building, health, and ADA codes.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain a federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) online through the California Secretary of State bizfile system, then apply for an EIN at irs.gov the same day. The EIN and entity name are prerequisites for the San Francisco business registration, the seller's permit, the bank account, and the lease signature.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate with the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector, obtaining a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at sftreasurer.org/business within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco. Pay the tiered registration fee (e.g., $55 for gross receipts up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, plus $4 state fee). The BAN is required by every other city department—Planning, Public Health, Building Inspection—so obtain it before filing any permit applications.

filing_playbook.action: File the fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the San Francisco County Clerk if the public-facing restaurant name differs from the legal entity name, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Bring the completed FBN form and photo ID to the County Clerk's office (City Hall, Room 168) or mail it with a check for the filing fee (approximately $60–$120). After filing, publish the statement in a San Francisco newspaper (e.g., the San Francisco Examiner or the San Francisco Chronicle) once a week for four consecutive weeks, then file the affidavit of publication with the Clerk within 45 days. Banks and the building permit application will require the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a California Seller's Permit with the Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) to collect sales tax on food and beverage sales.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online at onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov using the EIN and entity name. The permit is free and often issued the same day. CDTFA may request a security deposit depending on projected taxable sales; respond promptly with a sales forecast if requested. The seller's permit number must be displayed at the point of sale.

filing_playbook.action: Submit architectural plans for tenant improvements to the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection for a building permit, including DBI plan check, Planning zoning review (Section 175 referral), Public Health plan check, and any required plumbing, mechanical, and electrical permits pulled by…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire a California-licensed architect experienced with San Francisco restaurant build-outs to prepare a stamped plan set showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, three-compartment sink, hand-washing sinks, ADA-compliant restrooms, grease interceptor location, and occupant load calculation. Submit the plans to DBI with a Building Permit Application (BPA) designating 'health' and 'planning' as routing stations. In the cover letter reference the CUA case number (if applicable) and confirm that the proposed use is a restaurant with limited cooking. Request simultaneous DPH and Planning review to avoid serial delays. Budget 14–120 days for plan review depending on completeness and the number of correction rounds.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the Public Health Permit to Operate a food facility after the DPH plan check is approved, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and the space is ready for final inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online through the DPH Environmental Health portal at least one month before the target opening date, entering the BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY 2026–27 schedule; includes the initial inspection). Schedule the pre-opening inspection when the space is at least 80% complete—all equipment installed, surfaces sealed, hot water flowing, and a certified food safety manager certificate on file. Book the final inspection at least two weeks in advance. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization and the Health Permit to Operate, the two approvals in the entitlement path, and reflect the time to approval when those approvals are granted (not the time to a denial or withdrawal). The CUA timeline is estimated at 120–300 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing and final approval based on typical San Francisco hearing timelines for neighborhood commercial conditional use cases; the single comparable CUA in the candidate set (1988.272C at 2642 Ocean Ave) took 45 days in 1988, but that pre-dates current environmental review, neighborhood notification, and hearing-scheduling procedures. The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check is complete and prerequisites are met. The cost range includes the CUA filing fee (approximately $3,100 for a use decision without construction in 2024, CPI-adjusted annually per the Planning fee schedule), the health permit application fee ($470 for FY 2026–27), and the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant depending on complexity, FY 2026–27 schedule). Total estimated government fees for the two approvals are $4,400–$5,700. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) are not included because the building row has insufficient-information status, but they will add materially once the change-of-use determination is made. State and federal registrations (EIN, Secretary of State, seller's permit) add $70–$150 and take 1–10 days but are prerequisites, not approvals in the entitlement path.
